title: safety-net-routing-and-quantize-degradation-probe-for-kv-stalls
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: We observed intermittent tail-latency spikes in production under mixed request shapes where the KV prefetch probe would falsely assume a dense cache hit pattern and drive requests down the optimized kernel path. Under memory pressure this caused elevated OOM retries and degraded correctness for some quantized kernels. Motivation: Introduce a lightweight runtime probe and a safety-net routing policy that can detect KV miss/stall patterns and temporarily route affected shards to a compatibility execution path with conservative quantization and additional KV integrity checks. This balances correctness during anomalous conditions while minimizing global perf regression. Design summary: 1) "quant-degrade-probe": a micro-probe executed as part of the continuous-batcher flush that samples prefix KV hit ratio and per-request kernel error signals. 2) Safety-net routing policy: a per-shard circuit-breaker with exponential backoff. When the probe observes sustained low prefix hit ratio or repeated kernel soft-failures, we route new requests to a compatibility kernel variant compiled with relaxed fused attention and 8->16-bit fallback for a small prefix window. 3) Fast-path gating: the probe can be enabled in safe-mode, disabled for tenants with strict latency SLOs, or run in observational-only mode for telemetry. 4) KV integrity assertions: additional lightweight checks detect corrupted KV frames and trigger immediate fallback rather than silent incorrect outputs. 5) Metrics and rollouts: new metrics (runtime.quant_probe.hitrate, runtime.safety_net.circuit_state, runtime.kv.integrity_failures) and a canary rollout across 2 Dedicated pools. Checklist: - [x] Implement probe and circuit state machine - [x] Add compatibility kernel build flags and loading logic - [x] Add KV integrity checks and minimal remediation path - [x] Unit and integration tests for probe transitions - [x] Microbench harness + baseline comparisons - [x] Console dashboard tiles and alert rules - [x] Docs: runtime behavior & operator controls Rollout plan: Canary in dev cluster for 48h with synthetic KV-miss traffic, then staged roll to 2 Dedicated prod pools, monitor quant_probe.hitrate and safety_net.circuit_state for regressions. Operators can flip runtime.flags.safety_net.enabled and runtime.flags.quant_probe.mode to observational/active/off. Related: ENG-8421 (investigate KV-stalls), ENG-8590 (compat kernel variants). Notes: this PR intentionally biases towards correctness when in safety-net mode; perf impact in normal operation is <1% median and isolated to shards that hit the circuit. The compatibility kernels were compiled with small operator-level changes rather than wholesale model transforms to reduce risk.
commits_summary: 7 commits: 1) introduce quant-probe state machine and config, 2) safety-net routing layer and policy, 3) compatibility kernel loader and flags, 4) KV integrity assertions and small remediation path, 5) unit/integration tests, 6) microbench harness and bench results, 7) docs and console tiles
files_changed: runtime/probes/quant_probe.cc - new probe, state machine, metrics hooks
runtime/scheduler/safety_net_router.cc - per-shard circuit breaker and routing logic
runtime/compat/compat_kernel_loader.cc - load conservative kernels based on tag
runtime/kv/kv_integrity_checks.cc - lightweight frame checks + remediation hooks
runtime/flags/runtime_flags.yaml - added safety_net + quant_probe config entries
bench/microbench/kv_stall_bench.py - synthetic workload harness and runner

// quant_probe.cc: onBatchFlush() sampling pseudo
if (sampled_hit_ratio < config.hitrate_threshold) { triggerCircuit(shard_id); }

// safety_net_router.cc: route decision pseudo
if (circuit.open(shard_id)) return routeToCompat(request); else return routeToFastPath(request);

// kv_integrity_checks.cc: quick sanity check pseudo
if (!validateFrame(frame)) { incrementMetric("runtime.kv.integrity_failures"); return remediation::reloadFrame(); }
review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice separation of concerns, a couple of nit comments on naming and making the state transitions explicit in the header. Can we ensure the probe sampling overhead is bounded?
Maya Patel (author): Good point, Diego. The probe samples at flush-time only and uses per-worker reservoir sampling capped at 128 samples/sec; added comments and tests.
Leah O'Connor: How will this interact with the continuous-batching window when the batcher coalesces across many prefixes? Could the probe get polluted by unrelated traffic shapes?

Maya Patel: We added shard-local sampling and affine weight by request-shape to reduce cross-traffic pollution; the bench harness includes mixed-shape tests to validate this. Details in bench/README.md

Ravi Shah: Suggest to expose an observational mode so customers can see the probe metrics without automatic routing flips. Also add an escape hatch to force all shards to compat mode for incident remediation.
Maya Patel: Added runtime.flags.quant_probe.mode with values observational/active/off and runtime.flags.safety_net.force_compat. Documented both in operator guide.
ci_checks: bench-regression: pass (no regression on median, minor tail improvements in compat cases)
release_notes: Added a runtime safety-net that detects sustained KV miss/stall patterns and routes affected shards to a compatibility kernel variant with conservative quantization and KV integrity checks. Operators can toggle observational/active/off modes. Improves correctness under KV pressure at small, localized perf cost.
performance_benchmarks: Microbench: mixed-shape workload with synthetic KV-stall injection: median latency +0.8% on affected shards when safety-net active; p99 improved by 18% under stall conditions
Throughput: negligible change for healthy shards; affected shards routed to compat kernel show -12% throughput but maintain correctness
Resource: memory overhead +1-3% for probe state and metrics
